title: No, I don't have sisters!
html:
Modern dating blows, and many of its problems are summed up in this Reddit thread.

This exchange cracked me up:

It’s not just the men.

It’s not just the women.

It’s that there is an epidemic of poor communication skills, a culture that encourages relationship-killing behaviors, and an unwillingness of people to become the kind of people worth keeping around. Perhaps some women are playing hard to want, but you can bet that for every one of those, there’s (at least) one man playing hard to be with.

I’ve been on plenty of fruitless dates and been in a few relationships (with wonderful people, I might add), and what I’ve experienced largely aligns with the aforementioned Reddit post. Of the problems mentioned in the Reddit post, our society’s general lack of respect seems most pertinent. Without respect, all else fails.

I didn’t experience this lack of respect firsthand, however. I didn’t notice women being especially disrespectful to me, and I’m sure that I wasn’t to them (because of what I’m about to say). Strangely enough, I became aware of it partly through how many women thought I had sisters.

“Sooo… do you have any siblings?” she’d ask.

“Yeah. I’m the youngest of 3 boys.”

“Oh! I thought that you would’ve had at least one sister.”

Why though?

It turns out that these women assumed I had sisters because I was respectful and treated them like real human beings. What’s more interesting, and, perhaps, disheartening, is that common feedback I’ve gotten from past partners is some version of “Nobody has been so good to me before.”

It’s disheartening because I would never claim to be the poster child for chivalry and wooing. I’m not. After all, I’m single at the time of writing this. I’ve just been taught to treat people with respect, and, apparently, however I’ve treated these women was some combination of mind-blowing and confusing. They didn’t realize that being treated with such kindness and respect was an option.

So, men: Pull your heads out of your asses and be better.

If you're young enough (like me), there’s a good chance that you’re surrounded by degenerates who left their respect for humanity in their hometown before going to college.

Don’t be like them.

Be better. Be respectful. Be kind.

Join the movement of people trying to make it uncontroversial to say that not all men suck.

A lot of men suck. This is true. But you don’t have to be one.

And women: Well, I’ll leave it to you to figure out your problems. Just don’t go around pretending that you don’t have any (pssst… this might be one of your problems).

At the end of the day, life is best when we’re around wonderful people. So, it’s our responsibility to be wonderful.

“If you wanna make the world a better place
Take a look at yourself and then make a change.” — MJ
